rows.row: row = orient * 7 + cell index (orient = mirror*4 + rot, see shapes.json); rows 0-6 are rotation 0, the set asked for in the brief

notes: Skin for shaped cells (same sheet layout as walls_shapes.png). The cut edge (diagonal or arc) always faces space; mask bits say which FLAT edges also face space. Joint lines run on the top and left edges. Mask bit set = that side of the cell faces open SPACE (not "solid neighbour" as in walls.png): column = N*1 + E*2 + S*4 + W*8. The skin is drawn over a wall cell. It paints a rim (near-black outline, then a lit or shaded edge by facing) on every space-facing side and covers the cell up to 14px in from it, so the last 2px on the far side stay the wall's own interior outline; with no space-facing side (column 0) it is one whole panel. Cells on a thin spar that face space on two sides are covered fully.
